在1940年2月5日（星期一）上午10时于议事厅举行的会议上，出席者如下：

出席人员：
罗伯特·考尔德-马歇尔爵士，K.B.E.（主席）
孙 Russell Y. 先生（代表面粉厂主协会）
施 F. H. 先生（同上）
R. W. 约克先生（警务处助理总监）
T. W. 古布先生（副秘书）
何 T. K. 先生（副秘书），以及
T. 比斯利先生（供应小组委员会秘书）。

主席声明，召开此次会议旨在讨论当前面粉价格高企的局势，并探讨在面粉厂配合下，能否以更合理的价格获取面粉以满足本地需求。他表示，目前价格高昂，可供消费者的供应似乎不足，工部局亟盼尽可能改善这一状况。他邀请何先生开启讨论。

何先生表示，他知道在场的主要面粉厂代表均为具有公共精神的绅士，他深信他们将配合采取各项措施，以改善社区贫苦民众的境遇，从而协助维持上海的和平与良好秩序。何先生接着指出，各面粉厂向零售商的售价为每袋10.00元，但由于面粉厂每日向零售商提供的供应量远非充足，零售商报告称出现短缺并要求高价——目前市场价格为每袋11元，有时甚至高达11.50元。因此，恳请面粉厂主予以合作，并请他们允许增加供应量，以满足本地需求。

福丰面粉厂的孙 Russell 先生答复称，他可以毫无异议地断言，上海的面粉价格为全球最低。在天津和北京，价格约为每袋18元，而上海各面粉厂的售价为每袋10元，这是一种巨大的牺牲，他们觉得自己的举动已充分体现了公共精神。他说，上海各面粉厂每日销售面粉约3,000袋。在他看来，有人正在利用这一局势，并

（印：中文图书馆 ... I ... 146(1) ... 2/1 ... 4/c）

pages.en:
-2-
re-exporting. Mr. Russell Sun reports that his dealers are selling
through shops at $10.40 per bag and he states that he will be pleased
to furnish the names of all those to whom his Company allocates supplies
in order that a check can be made. As regards maintaining the price at
$10. per bag of flour (which figure is considered very low) he says
that it is not possible to continue selling at this price for long.
The new crop of domestic wheat is due in June and if it is not allowed
to come here freely the present low price cannot be expected. Continu-
ing Mr. Russell Sun says that at the moment foreign wheat costs $27.
per picul which when converted into flour would cost $13.50 per bag
without any profit to the Mills.

Mr. Ho states that he considers Mr. Russell Sun's offer to
provide the Council with a list of retail dealers who obtain stocks
from his Company (with prices shown etc.) a step in the right direction
and he hopes that Mr. Sze of the Foh Sing Mills will do likewise.
Mr. Sze says that his Company will be glad to afford such information.

The Chairman refers to the matter of re-exports and suggests
that if adequate information can be obtained ~~and~~ feasible steps
should be taken to check this practice. Mr. Ho in this connection
suggests that a condition of sale (imposed by the Mills) should
prevent, to a very large extent, re-exports. To this Mr. Russell Sun
states that dealers have been told time and again to distribute supplies
among real consumers. At one time, when the situation was acute, it was
hinted that if they did not take steps to prevent sales to speculators,
the Council might be given the quantity required by Shanghai and asked
to arrange for its distribution. These dealers, Mr. Russell Sun adds,
have received renewed warnings during the last two or three months.

Mr. F. H. Sze of the Foh Sing Mill, in reply to the Chairman's
invitation to express his views, states that as the food problem
affects the well-being of the community, before the plan of the sale
of cheap rice to the poor of Shanghai was commenced, his Company had
already adopted a scheme of selling a certain amount of flour at a price
far under their cost. This scheme has been continued up to the present
with admirable results and his Company is glad to continue it in spite
of the sacrifice which they are called upon to make. He is sorry
pages.zh:
-2-
再出口事宜。孙拉塞尔（Russell Sun）先生报告称，他的经销商正以每袋 10.40 美元的价格通过商店进行销售，并表示他乐意提供其公司分配供应品的所有对象名单，以便进行核查。关于将面粉价格维持在每袋 10.00 美元（该价格被认为非常低）的问题，他表示无法长期以此价格继续销售。国产小麦的新粮将于六月上市，如果不允许其自由运抵此处，则难以维持目前的低价。孙拉塞尔先生接着表示，目前外国小麦的价格为每担 27 美元，折算成面粉后，每袋成本将达 13.50 美元，面粉厂在此过程中毫无利润可言。

何先生表示，他认为孙拉塞尔先生提出向工部局提供从其公司获取库存的零售经销商名单（列明价格等）的举措是朝着正确方向迈出的一步，他希望福新面粉厂（Foh Sing Mills）的施先生也能采取同样做法。施先生表示，他的公司乐意提供此类信息。

主席提及再出口问题，并建议如果能获得充分的信息，~~并且~~应采取可行措施来遏制这种做法。对此，何先生建议，由面粉厂施加的销售条件应在很大程度上防止再出口行为。针对此点，孙拉塞尔先生表示，已多次告知经销商须将供应品分配给真正的消费者。在局势严峻时期，曾暗示如果他们不采取措施防止向投机者销售，工部局可能会获配上海所需的数量，并被要求安排分发。孙拉塞尔先生补充说，在过去两三个月里，这些经销商已再次收到警告。

福新面粉厂的施 F. H.（F. H. Sze）先生在回应主席邀请其发表意见时指出，鉴于粮食问题关乎社区福祉，在向上海贫民廉价出售大米的计划启动之前，他的公司已率先实施了一项方案，即以远低于成本的价格出售一定数量的面粉。该方案一直持续至今，成效卓著，尽管公司需为此作出牺牲，但仍乐意继续执行。他感到遗憾

pages.en:
-3-
however to say that his Company may not be able to continue this
service much longer. Continuing Mr. Sze says that since the fund
required for the sale of cheap rice to the poor can be collected by
means of contributions from various sources from time to time, it
can of course be carried on for a considerable period. However the
sale of cheap flour by his Company has to be limited by many
factors and he is afraid that his Company cannot do it for long
since their stock of flour will be exhausted and with very little
possibility of securing new raw materials in the future. He says
that his Company might manage to purchase foreign wheat again, but
every 133 lbs. of wheat thus purchased will cost some thirty
Shanghai dollars. Mr. Sze states that it will therefore be impossi-
ble for his Company to continue their scheme of selling their flour
at the present moderate price. If an attempt is made to raise their
price to such an extent as to enable them to cover their cost, he
is afraid many people, ignorant of their difficulties would
criticize them. He adds that his Company wishes to do their best
but they are confronted with a dilemma. He is glad to have this
opportunity of reporting something of the general condition of
their business and he will be glad if he can get some advice.
Mr. Ho says that he appreciates the Company's position.
Supposing that Shanghai's daily requirement is placed at 8,000 bags
of flour, then 240,000 bags would be needed monthly. According to
a report sent to the Council on January 6 by the Flour Mill Owners'
Association, the stock figure is given as 2½ million bags. So the
stock should last for approximately ten months if there is no
export, furthermore, the native wheat crop is due on the market
sometime in June. Mr. Ho therefore appeals to the Mill owners
present to allow Shanghai a greater quantity. Mr. Russell Sun
replies that from the figure of 2,500,000 bags of flour mentioned
by Mr. Ho, over 600,000 bags must be deducted to cover forward
commitments by his Mill and others who have contracts which must be
fulfilled.
pages.zh:
-3-
然而，他表示他的公司可能无法长期继续提供此项服务。施先生接着说，由于向穷人廉价出售大米所需的资金可以通过不时从各种来源募集捐款来筹集，因此这项业务当然可以维持相当长的一段时间。但是，他的公司廉价出售面粉的行为受到许多因素的限制，他担心公司无法长久维持，因为他们的面粉库存即将耗尽，而且未来获得新原料的可能性微乎其微。他说，他的公司或许能再次购买外国小麦，但每购买133磅这样的小麦，成本约为三十上海元。施先生表示，因此，他的公司不可能继续以目前的适中价格出售面粉的计划。如果试图将价格提高到足以弥补成本的程度，他担心许多不了解他们困难的人会批评他们。他补充说，他的公司希望尽力而为，但他们正面临两难境地。他很高兴有机会报告他们业务的一般状况，如果能得到一些建议，他将不胜感激。
何先生表示，他理解该公司的处境。假设上海的每日需求量为8,000袋面粉，那么每月就需要240,000袋。根据面粉厂主协会于1月6日提交给工部局的报告，库存数量为250万袋。因此，如果没有出口，库存应能维持大约十个月，此外，国产小麦将于六月某个时候上市。因此，何先生呼吁在场的面粉厂主允许向上海提供更多数量的面粉。孙拉塞尔先生回答说，从何先生提到的250万袋面粉的数字中，必须扣除超过60万袋，以履行他的工厂及其他有合同必须履行的厂商的远期承诺。

pages.en:
Mr. Ho states that these commitments have been made by the
Mills when they were quite aware that a system of permits for the export
of flour obtains and that the quota is decided upon monthly. Mr.
Russell Sun replies that these forward commitments were of course made
in anticipation of a continuance of the issue of permits; there was no
reason to believe that they would be discontinued.
    Mr. Ho asks if the Mills will disclose what profits they
made during 1939.
    Mr. Sze states that the stock of No.2 grade flour will soon
be exhausted, probably by February/March and in any case the Mills will
not be in a position to supply for long. He says that the reported
figures, quoted by Mr. Ho, do not include orders from dealers. He
agrees with the Chairman that the stock does not represent actual free
flour. Mr. Sze explains that the stock figure does not cover uncalled
delivery orders. The figures are not net but gross. Even at a figure
of 8,000 bags per day the Mills would not be able to supply for long.
    Mr. Ho states that the Chinese Press have criticised the
Flour trade for hoarding and the retailers have said that they get
insufficient stocks from the Mills. Mr. Russell Sun submits his
Company's stock list as also a statement of local consumption of
flour from his Mills. He reiterates that his Mills are only receiving
$10 per bag of flour and he adds that his Company has for the past three
years sold approximately 4,500 bags of flour daily for local consumption.
    The Chairman thanks Mr. Russell Sun for the very full informa-
tion given. He enquires whether in view of the shortage in rice stocks
more flour is being used. Mr. Russell Sun is unable to say what the
increase is while Mr. Yorke believes there has been a falling off since
the cheap sale of rice commenced.
    Mr. Russell Sun considers an estimate of 8,000 bags of Flour
sufficient for Shanghai's daily needs.
    Mr. Sze informs the meeting that local dealers will not buy
No.3 or 4 quality Flour which is cheaper than that quoted in the shops
which is for No.2 grade. He says that the consumption of flour appears
to be increasing, that Northern Chinese live on flour and Southerners on
Rice. He agrees with Mr. Ho that the Northern workers mainly depend on
flour.
pages.zh:
何先生指出，各面粉厂在作出这些远期承诺时，完全知晓当时实行面粉出口许可证制度，且配额系按月核定。孙乐斯（Russell Sun）先生答复称，作出这些远期承诺自然是基于对许可证持续签发的预期；没有任何理由相信许可证签发会中断。

何先生询问各面粉厂是否愿意披露其在 1939 年所获利润。

施先生表示，二号面粉的库存即将耗尽，可能就在二/三月间，无论如何，各面粉厂将无法长期维持供应。他指出，何先生所引用的报告数据并未包含来自经销商的订单。他同意主席的看法，即现有库存并不代表实际可用的自由流通面粉。施先生解释说，库存数据未涵盖尚未提货的交货单。这些数据是毛数而非净数。即使按每日 8,000 袋的数字计算，各面粉厂也无法长期维持供应。

何先生指出，中文报刊批评面粉业囤积居奇，零售商则称从面粉厂获得的库存不足。孙乐斯先生提交了其公司的库存清单，以及其面粉厂供本地消费的面粉情况说明。他重申，其面粉厂每袋面粉仅获利 10 元，并补充说，过去三年其公司每日约售出 4,500 袋面粉供本地消费。

主席感谢孙乐斯先生提供如此详尽的信息。他询问鉴于大米库存短缺，面粉的使用量是否有所增加。孙乐斯先生无法说明增长幅度，而约克（Yorke）先生认为，自大米低价抛售开始以来，面粉使用量反而有所下降。

孙乐斯先生认为，每日 8,000 袋面粉的估计数足以满足上海的日常需求。

施先生向会议通报，本地经销商不愿购买三号或四号面粉，尽管其价格低于商店中报价的二号面粉。他表示，面粉消费量似乎在增加，北方人以面粉为主食，南方人则以大米为主食。他同意何先生的看法，即北方籍工人主要依赖面粉为生。

pages.en:
The Chairman enquires as to the amount available daily from
their Mills.
Mr. Russell Sun replies that at $10 per bag Millers are
reluctant to sell because of the present cost of wheat. Some
Australian wheat is coming, but, as he has said, when it has been
milled it will cost considerably more than what is at present being
asked. He reports that he has 1,100,000 bags of flour and subtracting
from this figure undelivered orders, there will remain about 500,000
bags for the Shanghai Market as well as for export requirements.
Mr. Sze says that his Company's stocks, as will be seen by a
statement he produces, are very low amounting to 178,000 bags
(all grades).
The Chairman enquires as to the normal consumption of No.4
grade Flour and Mr. Russell Sun replies that Shanghai Chinese use flour
as a second foodstuff and not daily and No.4 grade Flour is not so
palatable as No.2 grade.
Mr. York remarks that Chinese feel that there must be no
meal if Flour only has been eaten; there must be rice to go with it,
and Flour goes towards the making of Hors d'Oeuvres.
Mr. Russell Sun points out that if the price of flour is
fixed at $10 (which it is impossible to do for any prolonged period)
there will be danger of stocks going beyond the Settlement jurisdiction
possibly to Peking and Tientsin where the price is at present $16 per
bag. He adds that a ban, for reasons known, has its dangers. His firm
has contracted to supply 340,000 bags of Flour for Tientsin and Peking
and most of this amount is for the Kailan Mining Administration for
their miners. The problem is interlocked. If Flour is denied the
cities mentioned there might be a complete stoppage of coal supplies
for Shanghai from these areas.
Mr. Ho wonders whether the Customs report that no foreign
Wheat has been received in Shanghai during the months September to
December 1939, is correct. Mr. Russell Sun answers that it is, but
some has arrived recently which is more costly and that from now to
next April only five cargoes have been placed and this is far below
requirements. Shanghai, he says, can not pay the price for Australian
Wheat and there is very little wheat coming from surrounding areas
pages.zh:
主席询问其面粉厂每日可供货的数量。

孙Russell先生回答说，由于目前小麦成本高昂，磨粉商不愿以每袋10美元的价格出售。一些澳大利亚小麦正在运抵，但正如他所说，这些小麦磨成面粉后的成本将远高于目前的要价。他报告称，他拥有110万袋面粉，从中扣除未交付的订单后，留给上海市场以及出口需求的大约还有50万袋。

施先生说，从他出示的一份报表可以看出，他公司的库存非常低，总计为17.8万袋（所有等级）。

主席询问4号面粉的正常消费量是多少，孙Russell先生回答说，上海华人将面粉作为第二种主食，并非每日食用，且4号面粉的口感不如2号面粉。

约克先生评论说，中国人认为如果只吃面粉而没有米饭搭配，就不算吃了一顿饭；必须配有米饭，而面粉主要用于制作点心。

孙Russell先生指出，如果将面粉价格固定在10美元（这在任何较长时期内都是不可能做到的），库存就有流出租界管辖范围的危险，可能流向目前价格为每袋16美元的北平和天津。他补充说，出于众所周知的原因，实施禁令存在风险。他的公司已签约向天津和北平供应34万袋面粉，其中大部分是供给开滦矿务总局用于其矿工。这个问题是相互关联的。如果上述城市无法获得面粉，上海来自这些地区的煤炭供应可能会完全中断。

何先生想知道，海关关于1939年9月至12月期间上海未收到任何外国小麦的报告是否准确。孙Russell先生回答说，该报告属实，但最近有一些小麦运抵，成本更高，而且从现在到明年四月仅安排了五批货物，这远低于需求量。他说，上海无力支付澳大利亚小麦的价格，而从周边地区运来的小麦也寥寥无几

pages.en:
-6-
of Shanghai.
Mr. Ho believes that the 2½ million bags of Flour in Shanghai
in January were obtained at a comparatively cheap cost and he considers
that local requirements should have first claim. To this Mr. Russell Sun
says that contracts amounting to 600,000 bags of Flour for outports must
be met; he asks if Mills are to be discouraged from importing wheat by
the imposition of an embargo on exports.
The Chairman says that he appreciates that if it had not been
for the importation of foreign wheat the situation would have been grave.
Mr. Ho informs the meeting that it has been reported to him
that huge bonuses have been paid to the staff of the Mills for 1939. In
the case of the Foh Sing Mills it is said that the bonus amounted to 14
years' pay. He asks whether this is so.
Mr. Russell Sun states that his Mills however did not pay that
amount and Mr. Sze says that he himself did not receive such a large
bonus.
Replying to the Chairman he agrees that the business has been
profitable and adds that salaries have been very low.
Mr. Ho says that it is not unreasonable for the Council to
request the Mills to look after local needs first. The Companies make
enormous profits because of local conditions. He suggests that they
should reduce their profits.
The Chairman enquires whether Mr. Ho meant that the Companies
should make more on Outport supplies. Mr. Ho said that local needs
should be met first although outport business is lucrative.
Mr. Russell Sun remarks that his Company is not making much on
forward sales. He enquires whether there was any intention to interfere
with legitimate business.
The Chairman replies that the aim is to secure stocks at the
most reasonable price possible for Shanghai. He suggests that a check
should be undertaken by the Police of Flour leaving Mills for the
Northern Markets.
The Secretary remarks that it is alleged by the Mills that
retailers are exporting and speculating and suggests they should receive
Police attention. The Chairman agrees.
pages.zh:
-6-
上海。

何先生认为，一月份上海的250万袋面粉是以相对低廉的成本获得的，他认为应优先满足本地需求。对此，孙乐士（Russell Sun）先生表示，必须履行总量达60万袋的面粉外埠供应合同；他询问，若实施出口禁令，是否会阻碍磨坊主进口小麦。

主席表示，他深知若非进口外国小麦，局势本会十分严峻。

何先生向会议通报，据向他报告，各磨坊已向员工发放了1939年度的巨额花红。据说福新磨坊（Foh Sing Mills）的花红数额相当于14年的薪水。他询问此事是否属实。

孙乐士先生声明，其旗下的磨坊并未支付如此数额的花红，施先生（Mr. Sze）也表示他自己并未收到如此巨额的奖金。

在回答主席的询问时，他承认该行业利润丰厚，并补充说薪资一直很低。

何先生表示，工部局要求磨坊优先照顾本地需求并非不合理。各公司因本地局势而获得了巨额利润。他建议它们应当降低利润。

主席询问何先生是否意指各公司应从外埠供应中获取更多利润。何先生表示，尽管外埠业务有利可图，但仍应首先满足本地需求。

孙乐士先生评论道，他的公司在远期销售中获利不多。他询问当局是否有意干预合法商业活动。

主席回答说，目标是以尽可能最合理的价格为上海确保库存。他建议由警务处对运往北方市场的面粉离开磨坊的情况进行检查。

秘书指出，据磨坊方面指控，零售商正在从事出口和投机活动，并建议警方应对此予以关注。主席表示同意。

pages.en:
Mr. Russell Sun suggests that the Council's policy and the
policy of the Mills for the next few months should be decided.
Mr. Sze submits a stock statement wherefrom it is noted that
the grand total of flour of all grades held by his Company is given at
178,250 bags nett after deducting forward sales. The statement also
shows the quantity and prices of Foreign wheat due in Shanghai in
April. The cost per picul of this wheat ranges from $26.33 to $29.07
or an average per picul of $28.00 to which must be added local delivery
charges of 0.25, allowance for loss of weight through transportation
of $0.55, bringing the cost of this wheat to $28.75 to which figure
must be added Manufacturing charges of $2.00 thus making the final
price per picul of $30.75!
Replying to the Chairman, Mr. Russell Sun states that his
500,000 bags previously mentioned include some foreign wheat which
is coming. He adds that his Company has 10,000 tons on order which
would produce about 350,000 bags of Flour.
The cost of this foreign flour will be at least $13.50 per
bag.
The Chairman says that if the price is fixed at $10 and it is
later decided to lift the embargo there would be a sudden rise.
Mr. Ho says that he does not favour price fixation. A more
abundant supply of Flour would bring prices down.
Mr. Russell Sun says not the price of foreign flour, for as
the Chairman is in a position to confirm, apart from the exchange
factor, freight and other charges have increased and shipping facili-
ties are difficult to secure.
In answer to the Chairman, Mr. Russell Sun says that the total
net amount of flour at present available to Shanghai is in the region
of 400,000 bags.
Mr. Sze states that local wheat dealers do not wish to sell
and are waiting for better prices. In reply to Mr. Yorko he says that
a quantity of this wheat is stored in the Settlement.
Mr. Ho remarks that about ten days ago the replacement cost
of flour was $11.60 to $11.70 per bag because the sale of wheat bran
covered the operating expenses of Mills. Mr. Russell Sun replies that
pages.zh:
孙乐斯（Russell Sun）先生建议，应决定工部局以及各面粉厂在未来几个月内的政策。

施先生提交了一份库存报表，从中可见，其公司持有的各级面粉总量在扣除远期销售后，净数为 178,250 袋。该报表还列明了四月份抵沪的外国小麦的数量及价格。此等小麦每担成本介于 26.33 美元至 29.07 美元之间，平均每担为 28.00 美元；此外须加上本地交货费 0.25 美元，以及运输途中重量损耗津贴 0.55 美元，致使该小麦成本达到 28.75 美元；在此数额上再加制造费 2.00 美元，故最终每担价格为 30.75 美元！

孙乐斯先生在回复主席时称，此前提及的 50,000 袋中包括部分即将运抵的外国小麦。他补充说，其公司已订购 10,000 吨，可生产约 350,000 袋面粉。

此种外国面粉的成本每袋至少为 13.50 美元。

主席表示，若将价格定为 10 美元，而后又决定解除禁令，则价格将会突然上涨。

何先生表示，他不赞成固定价格。面粉供应更加充足会使价格下降。

孙乐斯先生说，外国面粉的价格并非如此，正如主席所确认的那样，除汇率因素外，运费及其他费用均已上涨，且舱位难以获得。

孙乐斯先生在回答主席时表示，目前可供上海使用的面粉净总量约为 400,000 袋。

施先生指出，本地麦商不愿出售，正在等待更好的价格。在回复约科（Yorko）先生时，他表示部分此类小麦储存在租界内。

何先生评论道，大约十天前，面粉的重置成本为每袋 11.60 至 11.70 美元，因为麦麸的销售足以覆盖面粉厂的运营费用。孙乐斯先生回答说

pages.en:
-8-
this is so only to a certain extent and repeats that freight has
gone up and tonnage is short.
The Chairman says that he hopes the Mills will see that
all available flour finds its way into the Settlement and he is
sure that if needed the aid of the Police will be given. Mr. Yorke
concurs.
Mr. Russell Sun states that Mill owners feel that in fair-
ness the Council should issue a statement in order to make it known
that foreign flour costs $13 per bag at present.
Replying to Mr. Ho, Mr. Russell Sun says that the daily
quota for Shanghai if increased would go to hoarders. He says the
daily local consumption for the past three years has never
approached the figure given by the Police (20,000 bags). He agrees
with the Chairman that 7,000 to 8,000 bags per day would be about
correct. He mentions that the present price of Flour at $10 per
bag is cheaper than the price for rice. There has been a far
greater rise in the price to consumers of that food.
Mr. Ho agrees but requests that Shanghai be given a
greater supply in order to keep the price within reasonable bounds.
Mr. Russell Sun says that apart from other factors, if
this is done Shanghai Mills would be exhausted and the cost of Flour
would then reach $15 per bag.
The Chairman remarks that no increase of Stocks to bring
about such a state is desired but just a little more is needed, say
a total of 10,000 bags daily for Shanghai.
Mr. Russell Sun repeats that the more free flour there is
the more will be exported from areas beyond the Council's control.
The Chairman says that this would be so unless steps can be taken
to prevent movement beyond the jurisdiction of the Settlement and
French Concession.
Mr. Russell Sun considers that 8,000 bags is sufficient
and should be the limit; his Company can allow 250,000 bags of Flour
for Shanghai needs for the next few months.
Mr. Ho says that he would be happy if Mr. Russell Sun would
make a larger offer and he would prefer him to say how much his
Company is prepared to allow daily for Shanghai.
pages.zh:
-8-
这种情况仅在某种程度上属实，并重申运费已上涨，且吨位不足。
主席表示，他希望各面粉厂能确保所有可用面粉均运入租界，并确信如有需要，警方将提供协助。约克先生（Mr. Yorke）表示赞同。
孙乐斯尔先生（Mr. Russell Sun）指出，面粉厂主认为，为公平起见，工部局应发表一项声明，以告知公众目前外国面粉每袋价格为13美元。
在回复何先生（Mr. Ho）时，孙乐斯尔先生表示，如果增加上海的每日配额，这些面粉将落入囤积者手中。他说，过去三年上海本地的每日消费量从未达到警方给出的数字（20,000袋）。他同意主席的看法，即每日7,000至8,000袋大致准确。他提到，目前面粉每袋10美元的价格比米价更便宜。而该食品对消费者的价格涨幅要大得多。
何先生表示同意，但要求增加对上海的供应，以便将价格保持在合理范围内。
孙乐斯尔先生表示，除其他因素外，如果这样做，上海的面粉厂库存将耗尽，届时面粉成本将达到每袋15美元。
主席评论说，并不希望通过增加库存来达到这种地步，只是需要稍微多一点，例如上海每日总量为10,000袋。
孙乐斯尔先生重申，自由流通的面粉越多，从工部局管辖区域以外地区出口的面粉就越多。
主席表示，除非能采取措施防止物资流动超出公共租界和法租界的管辖范围，否则情况确会如此。
孙乐斯尔先生认为8,000袋已足够，并应作为上限；他的公司可以在未来几个月内为上海的需求提供250,000袋面粉。
何先生表示，如果孙乐斯尔先生能提供更大的供应量，他将感到高兴，并且他更希望孙先生说明其公司准备每日允许向上海供应多少面粉。

pages.en:
-9-

Mr. Russell Sun offers 5,000 bags of Flour daily up to a total of 250,000 bags for Shanghai's requirements. Turning to Mr. Sze, Mr. Ho enquires whether he is willing to allow a similar amount from his Mills, to which Mr. Sze replies that he is unable to commit his Company and remarks that his Company's stocks are low.

Mr. Ho says that supposing the Mills are prepared to supply 20,000 bags of Flour of 49 lbs. which the Police estimate is required every day, then 980,000 people will get 1 lb. each a day, and since the present estimated population is about 4 million, then the needs of a quarter of the population will be met.

Mr. Sze repeats that he cannot commit his Company whereupon Mr. Ho undertakes to make a personal appeal to Mr. Wang Yi-Ching, General Manager of the Foh Sing Mills which Mr. Sze represents.

It is finally agreed
That the Mills will furnish the Police daily with lists of shops showing their addresses and the quantity of Flour supplied to them by the Mills.

In answer to Mr. Yorke, Mr. Sze says the lists would include about 100 shops.

In reply to the Chairman's query, Mr. Yorke says that the Settlement Police will keep the French Police posted as to what has been agreed and there will be close co-operation.

Replying to the Chairman on the matter of price, Mr. Russell Sun states that he can only supply a total of 250,000 bags of Flour at the rate of 5,000 bags daily for the next 50 days, and the cost will be $10 per bag - this is at a great sacrifice.

Mr. Ho asks whether the retail prices should be fixed. Mr. Russell Sun suggests that Retailers should sell at from $10.20 to $10.30 per bag of 49 lbs. He considers that 30 cents per bag is a very good profit for them. Mr. Sze agrees.

The Chairman enquires what action will be taken against hoarders and speculators. Mr. Yorke replies that if adequate proof is forthcoming they would be charged.
pages.zh:
-9-

孙Russell先生提出，为满足上海的需求，每日供应5,000袋面粉，总计250,000袋。何先生转而询问施先生是否愿意从其面粉厂提供同等数量的面粉，施先生答复称他无法代表其公司作出承诺，并指出其公司库存偏低。

何先生表示，假设各面粉厂愿意供应警方估算的每日所需之49磅装面粉20,000袋，那么每日将有98万人每人获得1磅面粉；鉴于目前估计人口约为400万，这将满足四分之一人口的需求。

施先生重申他无法代表其公司作出承诺，于是何先生承诺将亲自向施先生所代表的福新面粉厂（Foh Sing Mills）总经理王义庆先生提出请求。

最终议定：
各面粉厂将每日向警方提供一份商店名单，列明其地址及由面粉厂向其供应的面粉数量。

针对约克先生的提问，施先生表示该名单将包含约100家商店。

回应主席的询问，约克先生表示，租界警方会将已达成的协议内容通报法国警方，双方将进行密切合作。

就价格问题回答主席时，孙Russell先生声明，他在接下来的50天内，按每日5,000袋的速度，仅能供应总计250,000袋面粉，价格为每袋10美元——这是巨大的牺牲。

何先生询问是否应固定零售价格。孙Russell先生建议零售商以每袋49磅10.20至10.30美元的价格出售。他认为每袋30美分的利润对他们来说已相当可观。施先生表示同意。

主席询问将对囤积居奇者和投机者采取何种行动。约克先生答复称，如果有充分的证据，将对他们提起诉讼。

pages.en:
-10-

Mr. Ho undertakes to get in touch with the retail dealers
through the Rice Guild since there is no Association of Flour shops
and most retailers also deal in Rice. He will inform them of what
has been decided.

Mr. Russell Sun expresses the hope that in order to
remove criticism the Council will give some publicity to what has
been promised.

The Chairman thanks Mr. Russell Sun and Mr. Sze for their
attendance and assistance.

The meeting terminates at 11.40 a.m.
pages.zh:
-10-

何先生承诺，由于不存在面粉店同业公会，且大多数零售商也经营大米，他将通过米业公会与零售商人取得联系。他将向他们通报已作出的决定。

孙乐斯（Russell Sun）先生表示希望，为消除批评，工部局应对已承诺的事项进行一些公开宣传。

主席感谢孙乐斯先生和施先生（Sze）的出席与协助。

会议于上午11时40分结束。

pages.en:
FILE
At a meeting held in the Council Chamber on Monday, February 5, 1940, at
10 a.m. there are:-
8039A/S/3)
9 2 40
Present:
Sir Robert Calder-Marshall, K.B.E. (In the Chair)
Messrs. Russell Y. Sun (representing the Flour Mill
Owners' Association)
F. H. Sze ( do )
Mr. R. W. Yorke (Assistant Commissioner of Police)
Mr. T. W. Gubb (Deputy Secretary)
Mr. T. K. Ho (Deputy Secretary), and
Mr. T. Beesley (Secretary, Supplies Sub-Committee).
The Chairman states that the meeting has been called to
discuss the situation as regards the present high price of Flour
and to see if, with the co-operation of the Mills, flour can be
got for local needs at a more reasonable price. He says that the
present price is high, supplies available for consumers appear to be
inadequate and the Council is anxious to improve the situation if
possible. He invites Mr. Ho to open the discussion.
Mr. Ho says that he knows that the representatives of the
leading mills who are present are public spirited gentlemen and he
feels confident that they will co-operate in steps to be taken to
ameliorate the lot of the poor of the community thereby assisting
in the maintenance of peace and good order in Shanghai. Continuing
Mr. Ho states that Mills are selling flour to retail dealers at
$10.00 per bag but as the daily supply to them from Mills is far
from adequate, retailers report a shortage and ask for high prices
-- the present market price is $11. and sometimes as much as $11.50
per bag. The co-operation of Mill-owners is therefore requested
and they are asked to allow larger supplies to meet local requirements.
Mr. Russell Sun (of the Fou Foong Flour Mill) in reply
states that he can say without fear of contradiction, that
Shanghai's price for flour is the lowest in the world. In Tientsin
and Peking it stands at about $18. per bag while Shanghai Mills are
selling at $10. per bag which is a big sacrifice and they feel
that they have been quite public spirited in their action. He says
that about 8,000 bags of flour are sold daily in Shanghai by the
Mills. In his view some one is taking advantage of the situation and
(印：INITIALED BY
(S.H.) R.C.M.
DATE 7/2/40)
pages.zh:
档案

在1940年2月5日（星期一）上午10时于议事厅举行的会议上，出席者如下：-
8039A/S/3)
9 2 40

出席人员：
罗伯特·考尔德-马歇尔爵士，K.B.E.（主席）
孙 Russell Y. 先生（代表面粉厂主协会）
施 F. H. 先生（同上）
R. W. 约克先生（警务处助理总监）
T. W. 古布先生（副秘书）
何 T. K. 先生（副秘书），以及
T. 比斯利先生（供应小组委员会秘书）。

主席声明，召开此次会议旨在讨论当前面粉价格高企的局势，并探讨能否在面粉厂的配合下，以更合理的价格获取面粉以满足本地需求。他表示，目前价格高昂，可供消费者的供应似乎不足，工部局亟望尽可能改善这一局面。他邀请何先生开启讨论。

何先生表示，他知道在座的几家主要面粉厂代表均为具有公共精神的绅士，他深信他们将配合采取相关措施，以改善社区贫苦民众的境遇，从而协助维持上海的和平与良好秩序。何先生接着指出，各面粉厂向零售商贩出售面粉的价格为每袋10.00元，但由于面粉厂每日向零售商提供的供应量远未充足，零售商报告称出现短缺，并索要高价——目前的市场价格为每袋11元，有时甚至高达11.50元。因此，恳请面粉厂主予以合作，并要求他们增加供应量以满足本地需求。

福丰面粉厂的孙 Russell 先生答复称，他可以毫无异议地断言，上海的面粉价格是全球最低的。在天津和北京，价格约为每袋18元，而上海的面粉厂售价为每袋10元，这是一个巨大的牺牲，他们觉得自己的举动已充分体现了公共精神。他说，上海的面粉厂每日销售面粉约8,000袋。在他看来，有人正在利用这一局势，并
（印：由以下人员简签
(S.H.) R.C.M.
日期 1940年2月7日）

pages.en:
-2-
re-exporting. Mr. Russell Sun reports that his dealers are selling
through shops at $10.40 per bag and he states that he will be pleased
to furnish the names of all those to whom his Company allocates supplies
in order that a check can be made. As regards maintaining the price at
$10. per bag of flour (which figure is considered very low) he says
that it is not possible to continue selling at this price for long.
The new crop of domestic wheat is due in June and if it is not allowed
to come here freely the present low price cannot be expected. Continu-
ing Mr. Russell Sun says that at the moment foreign wheat costs $27.
per picul which when converted into flour would cost $13.50 per bag
without any profit to the Mills.

Mr. Ho states that he considers Mr. Russell Sun's offer to
provide the Council with a list of retail dealers who obtain stocks
from his Company (with prices shown etc.) a step in the right direction
and he hopes that Mr. Sze of the Foh Sing Mills will do likewise.
Mr. Sze says that his Company will be glad to afford such information.

The Chairman refers to the matter of re-exports and suggests
that if adequate information can be obtained and feasible steps
should be taken to check this practice. Mr. Ho in this connection
suggests that a condition of sale (imposed by the Mills) should
prevent, to a very large extent, re-exports. To this Mr. Russell Sun
states that dealers have been told time and again to distribute supplies
among real consumers. At one time, when the situation was acute, it was
hinted that if they did not take steps to prevent sales to speculators,
the Council might be given the quantity required by Shanghai and asked
to arrange for its distribution. These dealers, Mr. Russell Sun adds,
have received renewed warnings during the last two or three months.

Mr. F. H. Sze of the Foh Sing Mill, in reply to the Chairman's
invitation to express his views, states that as the food problem
affects the well-being of the community, before the plan of the sale
of cheap rice to the poor of Shanghai was commenced, his Company had
already adopted a scheme of selling a certain amount of flour at a price
far under their cost. This scheme has been continued up to the present
with admirable results and his Company is glad to continue it in spite
of the sacrifice which they are called upon to make. He is sorry
pages.zh:
-2-
再出口事宜。孙拉塞尔（Russell Sun）先生报告称，其经销商正以每袋 10.40 美元的价格通过商店销售，并表示他乐意提供其公司分配供应品的所有对象名单，以便进行核查。关于将面粉价格维持在每袋 10.00 美元（该价格被认为非常低）的问题，他表示无法长期以此价格继续销售。国产小麦的新收成将于六月上市，如果允许其自由运抵此处，则目前的低价恐难维持。孙拉塞尔先生接着表示，目前进口小麦价格为每担 27 美元，折算成面粉后，每袋成本为 13.50 美元，面粉厂在此过程中无任何利润。

何先生表示，他认为孙拉塞尔先生提出向工部局提供从其公司获取库存的零售经销商名单（列明价格等）之举是朝着正确方向迈出的一步，他希望福新面粉厂（Foh Sing Mills）的施先生也能采取同样做法。施先生表示，其公司乐意提供此类信息。

主席提及再出口事宜，并建议若能获得充分信息，应采取可行步骤遏制此种做法。对此，何先生建议，由面粉厂施加的销售条件应在很大程度上防止再出口。针对此点，孙拉塞尔先生表示，已多次告知经销商须将供应品分配给真正的消费者。曾在局势严峻之时，有人暗示若他们不采取措施防止向投机者销售，工部局可能会获配上海所需的数量，并被要求安排分发。孙拉塞尔先生补充说，在过去两三个月里，这些经销商已再次收到警告。

福新面粉厂的施 F. H.（F. H. Sze）先生在回应主席邀请其发表意见时表示，鉴于粮食问题关乎社区福祉，在向上海贫民廉价出售大米的计划启动之前，其公司已率先实施了一项以远低于成本的价格出售一定数量面粉的方案。该方案一直持续至今，成效卓著，尽管需作出牺牲，其公司仍乐意继续执行。他感到遗憾

pages.en:
-3-
however to say that his Company may not be able to continue this
service much longer. Continuing Mr. Sze says that since the fund
required for the sale of cheap rice to the poor can be collected by
means of contributions from various sources from time to time, it
can of course be carried on for a considerable period. However the
sale of cheap flour by his Company has to be limited by many
factors and he is afraid that his Company cannot do it for long
since their stock of flour will be exhausted and with very little
possibility of securing new raw materials in the future. He says
that his Company might manage to purchase foreign wheat again, but
every 133 lbs. of wheat thus purchased will cost some thirty
Shanghai dollars. Mr. Sze states that it will therefore be impossi-
ble for his Company to continue their scheme of selling their flour
at the present moderate price. If an attempt is made to raise their
price to such an extent as to enable them to cover their cost, he
is afraid many people, ignorant of their difficulties would
criticize them. He adds that his Company wishes to do their best
but they are confronted with a dilemma. He is glad to have this
opportunity of reporting something of the general condition of
their business and he will be glad if he can get some advice.
Mr. Ho says that he appreciates the Company's position.
Supposing that Shanghai's daily requirement is placed at 8,000 bags
of flour, then 240,000 bags would be needed monthly. According to
a report sent to the Council on January 6 by the Flour Mill Owners'
Association, the stock figure is given as 2½ million bags. So the
stock should last for approximately ten months if there is no
export, furthermore, the native wheat crop is due on the market
sometime in June. Mr. Ho therefore appeals to the Mill owners
present to allow Shanghai a greater quantity. Mr. Russell Sun
replies that from the figure of 2,500,000 bags of flour mentioned
by Mr. Ho, over 600,000 bags must be deducted to cover forward
commitments by his Mill and others who have contracts which must be
fulfilled.
pages.zh:
-3-
然而，他说他的公司可能无法再长期维持这项服务。施先生接着说，由于向穷人廉价出售大米所需的资金可以通过不时从各种来源募集捐款来筹集，因此这项服务当然可以持续相当长的一段时间。但是，他的公司廉价出售面粉的做法受到许多因素的限制，他担心公司无法长久维持，因为他们的面粉库存即将耗尽，而且未来获得新原料的可能性微乎其微。他说，他的公司或许能再次购买外国小麦，但每购买133磅这样的小麦，成本约为三十上海元。施先生表示，因此，他的公司不可能继续以目前的适中价格出售面粉的计划。如果试图提高价格至足以覆盖成本的程度，他担心许多不了解他们困难的人会批评他们。他补充说，他的公司希望尽力而为，但他们正面临两难境地。他很高兴有机会报告他们业务的一般状况，如果能得到一些建议，他将不胜感激。
何先生表示，他理解该公司的处境。假设上海的每日需求量为8,000袋面粉，那么每月就需要240,000袋。根据面粉厂主协会于1月6日向工部局董事会提交的一份报告，库存数量列为250万袋。因此，如果没有出口，库存应能维持大约十个月；此外，国产小麦作物将于六月某个时候上市。因此，何先生呼吁在场的面粉厂主允许向上海提供更多数量的面粉。孙罗素先生回答说，从何先生提到的250万袋面粉的数字中，必须扣除超过60万袋，以履行他的工厂及其他签订有必须履行合同者的远期承诺。

pages.en:
-4-
Mr. Ho states that these commitments have been made by the
Mills when they were quite aware that a system of permits for the export
of flour obtains and that the quota is decided upon monthly. Mr.
Russell Sun replies that these forward commitments were of course made
in anticipation of a continuance of the issue of permits; there was no
reason to believe that they would be discontinued.
Mr. Ho asks if the Mills will disclose what profits they
made during 1939.
Mr. Sze states that the stock of No.2 grade flour will soon
be exhausted, probably by February/March and in any case the Mills will
not be in a position to supply for long. He says that the reported
figures, quoted by Mr. Ho, do not include orders from dealers. He
agrees with the Chairman that the stock does not represent actual free
flour. Mr. Sze explains that the stock figure does not cover uncalled
delivery orders. The figures are not net but gross. Even at a figure
of 8,000 bags per day the Mills would not be able to supply for long.
Mr. Ho states that the Chinese Press have criticised the
Flour trade for hoarding and the retailers have said that they got
insufficient stocks from the Mills. Mr. Russell Sun submits his
Company's stock list as also a statement of local consumption of
flour from his Mills. He reiterates that his Mills are only receiving
$10 per bag of flour and he adds that his Company has for the past three
years sold approximately 4,500 bags of flour daily for local consumption.
The Chairman thanks Mr. Russell Sun for the very full informa-
tion given. He enquires whether in view of the shortage in rice stocks
more flour is being used. Mr. Russell Sun is unable to say what the
increase is while Mr. Yorke believes there has been a falling off since
the cheap sale of rice commenced.
Mr. Russell Sun considers an estimate of 8,000 bags of Flour
sufficient for Shanghai's daily needs.
Mr. Sze informs the meeting that local dealers will not buy
No.3 or 4 quality Flour which is cheaper than that quoted in the shops
which is for No.2 grade. He says that the consumption of flour appears
to be increasing, that Northern Chinese live on flour and Southerners on
Rice. He agrees with Mr. Ho that the Northern workers mainly depend on
flour.
pages.zh:
-4-
何先生指出，各面粉厂在作出这些远期承诺时，完全知晓面粉出口实行许可证制度，且配额系按月核定。孙乐斯（Russell Sun）先生答复称，作出这些远期承诺自然是基于对许可证将继续签发的预期；没有任何理由相信许可证签发会中止。

何先生询问各面粉厂是否愿意披露其在 1939 年所获利润。

施先生表示，二号面粉的库存即将耗尽，可能就在二月或三月，无论如何，各面粉厂将无法长期维持供应。他说，何先生所引用的报告数据并未包含来自经销商的订单。他同意主席的看法，即库存数据并不代表实际可用的自由面粉。施先生解释说，库存数字未涵盖尚未要求提货的交货单。这些数字是毛数而非净数。即使按每日 8,000 袋的数字计算，各面粉厂也无法长期维持供应。

何先生指出，中文报纸批评面粉业囤积居奇，零售商则称从面粉厂获得的库存不足。孙乐斯先生提交了其公司的库存清单，以及其面粉厂供本地消费的面粉情况说明。他重申，其面粉厂每袋面粉仅获利 10 元，并补充说，其公司在过去三年中，每天约出售 4,500 袋面粉供本地消费。

主席感谢孙乐斯先生提供的详尽信息。他询问，鉴于大米库存短缺，面粉的使用量是否有所增加。孙乐斯先生无法说明增加的具体幅度，而约克（Yorke）先生则认为，自大米低价销售开始以来，面粉使用量已出现下降。

孙乐斯先生认为，每日 8,000 袋面粉的估计数足以满足上海的每日需求。

施先生向会议通报，本地经销商不愿购买三号或四号面粉，尽管其价格比商店中报价的二号面粉便宜。他说，面粉消费量似乎在增加，北方人以面粉为主食，南方人则以大米为主食。他同意何先生的看法，即北方工人主要依赖面粉。

pages.en:
-5-
The Chairman enquires as to the amount available daily from
their Mills.
Mr. Russell Sun replies that at $10 per bag Mills are
reluctant to sell because of the present cost of wheat. Some
Australian wheat is coming, but, as he has said, when it has been
milled it will cost consumers much more than what is at present being
asked. He reports that he has 1,100,000 bags of flour and subtracting
from this figure undelivered orders, there will remain about 500,000
bags for the Shanghai Market as well as for export requirements.
Mr. Sze says that his Company's stocks, as will be observed
from a statement he produces, are very low amounting to 178,000 bags
(all grades).
The Chairman enquires as to the normal consumption of No.4
grade Flour and Mr. Russell Sun replies that Shanghai Chinese use flour
as a second foodstuff and not daily and No.4 grade Flour is not as
palatable as No.2 grade.
Mr. Yorke remarks that Chinese feel that there has been no
meal if Flour only has been eaten; there must be rice to be a meal,
and Flour goes towards the making of Hors d'Oeuvres.
Mr. Russell Sun points out that if the price of Flour is
fixed at $10 (which it is impossible to do for any prolonged period)
there will be danger of stocks going beyond the Settlement jurisdiction
possibly to Peking and Tientsin where the price is at present $18 per
bag. He adds that a ban, for reasons known, has its dangers. His firm
has contracted to supply 340,000 bags of Flour for Tientsin and Peking
and most of this amount is for the Kailan Mining Administration for
their miners. The problem is interlocked. If Flour is denied the
cities mentioned there might be a complete stoppage of coal supplies
for Shanghai from these areas.
Mr. Ho wonders whether the Customs report that no foreign
wheat has been received in Shanghai during the months September to
December 1939, is correct. Mr. Russell Sun answers that it is, but
some has arrived recently which is more costly and that from now to
next April only five cargoes have been placed and this is far below
requirements. Shanghai, he says, can not pay the price for Australian
wheat and there is very little wheat coming from the surrounding areas
pages.zh:
-5-
主席询问其面粉厂每日可供货的数量。

孙乐斯（Russell Sun）先生回答说，由于目前小麦成本高昂，各面粉厂不愿以每袋 10 元的价格出售。一些澳大利亚小麦正在运抵，但正如他此前所言，这些小麦磨成面粉后，消费者所需支付的费用将远高于目前的要价。他报告称，他拥有 110 万袋面粉，从中扣除未交付的订单后，剩余约 50 万袋可供上海市场及出口需求。

施（Sze）先生指出，从他提交的报表中可以看出，他公司的库存非常低，仅为 178,000 袋（所有等级）。

主席询问 4 号面粉的正常消费量是多少，孙乐斯先生回答说，上海华人将面粉作为第二种主食，并非每日食用，且 4 号面粉的口感不如 2 号面粉。

约克（Yorke）先生评论道，中国人认为如果只吃面粉而不吃米饭，就不算是一顿饭；必须有米饭才构成一顿正餐，而面粉主要用于制作点心（Hors d'Oeuvres）。

孙乐斯先生指出，如果将面粉价格固定在 10 元（这在任何较长时期内都是不可能做到的），则存在库存流出租界管辖范围的危险，可能会流向目前价格为每袋 18 元的北平和天津。他补充说，出于众所周知的原因，实施禁令是有风险的。他的公司已签订合同，向北平和天津供应 340,000 袋面粉，其中大部分是供给开滦矿务总局（Kailan Mining Administration）用于其矿工。这个问题是相互关联的。如果上述城市无法获得面粉，可能会导致这些地区向上海的煤炭供应完全中断。

何（Ho）先生想知道，海关关于 1939 年 9 月至 12 月期间上海未收到任何外国小麦的报告是否准确。孙乐斯先生回答说，该报告属实，但最近已有一些小麦运抵，其价格更为昂贵，而且从现在到明年四月之间仅安排了五批货物，这远远低于需求量。他说，上海无力支付澳大利亚小麦的价格，而从周边地区运来的小麦也寥寥无几

pages.en:
of Shanghai.
-6-
Mr. Ho believes that the 2½ million bags of Flour in Shanghai
in January were obtained at a comparatively cheap cost and he considers
that local requirements should have first claim. To this Mr. Russell Sun
says that contracts amounting to 600,000 bags of Flour for outports must
be met; he asks if Mills are to be discouraged from importing wheat by
the imposition of an embargo on exports.
The Chairman says that he appreciates that if it had not been
for the importation of foreign wheat the situation would have been grave.
Mr. Ho informs the meeting that it has been reported to him
that huge bonuses have been paid to the staff of the Mills for 1939. In
the case of the Foh Sing Mills it is said that the bonus amounted to 14
years pay. He asks whether this is so.
Mr. Russell Sun states that his Mills however did not pay that
amount, and Mr. Sze says that he himself did not receive such a large
bonus.
Replying to the Chairman he agrees that the business has been
profitable and adds that salaries have been very low.
Mr. Ho says that it is not unreasonable for the Council to
request the Mills to look after local needs first. The Companies make
enormous profits because of local conditions. He suggests that they
should reduce their profits.
The Chairman enquires whether Mr. Ho meant that the Companies
should make more on Outport supplies. Mr. Ho said that local needs
should be met first although outport business is lucrative.
Mr. Russell Sun remarks that his Company is not making much on
forward sales. He enquires whether there was any intention to interfere
with legitimate business.
The Chairman replies that the aim is to secure stocks at the
most reasonable price possible for Shanghai. He suggests that a check
should be undertaken by the Police of Flour leaving Mills for the
Northern Markets.
The Secretary remarks that it is alleged by the Mills that
retailers are exporting and speculating and suggests they should receive
Police attention. The Chairman agrees.
pages.zh:
上海。
-6-
何先生认为，一月份上海的250万袋面粉是以相对低廉的成本获得的，他认为应优先满足本地需求。对此，孙乐斯（Russell Sun）先生表示，必须履行总计60万袋面粉的外埠合同；他询问，若实施出口禁令，是否会阻碍面粉厂进口小麦。

主席表示，他认识到，若非进口外国小麦，局势本将十分严峻。

何先生向会议通报，据向他报告，各面粉厂员工已获发1939年度的巨额花红。据说福新面粉公司（Foh Sing Mills）的花红数额相当于14年的薪水。他询问此事是否属实。

孙乐斯先生声明，他的面粉厂并未支付如此数额的花红，施先生（Sze）也表示他自己并未收到如此巨额的奖金。

在回答主席的询问时，他同意该行业利润丰厚，并补充说薪资一直很低。

何先生表示，工部局要求面粉厂优先照顾本地需求并非不合理。各公司因本地局势而获得巨额利润。他建议它们应降低利润。

主席询问何先生是否意指各公司应从外埠供应中获取更多利润。何先生表示，尽管外埠业务利润丰厚，但仍应首先满足本地需求。

孙乐斯先生评论说，他的公司在远期销售中获利不多。他询问是否有意干涉正当商业活动。

主席回答说，目标是以尽可能合理的价格为上海确保库存。他建议由警务处对运往北方市场的面粉离开面粉厂的情况进行检查。

秘书指出，据面粉厂指控，零售商正在从事出口和投机活动，并建议警方应对此予以关注。主席表示同意。

pages.en:
-7-

Mr. Russell Sun suggests that the Council's policy and the
policy of the Mills for the next few months should be decided.
Mr. Sze submits a stock statement wherefrom it is noted that
the grand total of flour of all grades held by his Company is given at
178,250 bags nett after deducting forward sales; The statement also
shows the quantity and prices of Foreign wheat due in Shanghai in
April. The cost per picul of this wheat ranges from $26.33 to $29.07
or an average per picul of $28.00 to which must be added local delivery
charges of 0.25, allowance for loss of weight through transportation
of $0.55, bringing the cost of this wheat to $28.75 to which figure
must be added Manufacturing charges of $2.00 thus making the final
price per picul of $30.75.

Replying to the Chairman, Mr. Russell Sun states that his
500,000 bags previously mentioned include some foreign wheat which
is coming. He adds that his Company has 10,000 tons on order which
would produce about 350,000 bags of Flour.

The cost of this foreign flour will be at least $13.50 per
bag.

The Chairman says that if the price is fixed at $10 and it is
later decided to lift the embargo there would be a sudden rise.

Mr. Ho says that he does not favour price fixation. A more
abundant supply of Flour would bring prices down.

Mr. Russell Sun says not the price of foreign flour, for as
the Chairman is in a position to confirm, apart from the exchange
factor, freight and other charges have increased and shipping facili-
ties are difficult to secure.

In answer to the Chairman, Mr. Russell Sun says that the total
net amount of flour at present available to Shanghai is in the region
of 400,000 bags.

Mr. Sze states that local Wheat dealers do not wish to sell
and are waiting for better prices. In reply to Mr. York he says that
a quantity of this wheat is stored in the Settlement.

Mr. Ho remarks that about ten days ago the replacement cost
of flour was $11.60 to $11.70 per bag because the sale of wheat bran
covered the operating expenses of Mills. Mr. Russell Sun replies that
pages.zh:
-7-

孙乐斯（Russell Sun）先生建议，应决定工部局以及各面粉厂在未来数月内的政策。

施先生提交了一份库存报表，从中可见，扣除远期销售后，其公司持有的各级面粉总量为 178,250 袋（净重）。该报表还列明了四月份抵沪的外国小麦的数量及价格。此等小麦每担成本在 26.33 美元至 29.07 美元之间，平均每担 28.00 美元；此外须加上本地交货费 0.25 美元，以及运输途中重量损耗补贴 0.55 美元，致使该小麦成本达到 28.75 美元；在此数额上再加制造费 2.00 美元，故最终价格为每担 30.75 美元。

针对主席的提问，孙乐斯先生表示，此前提到的 500,000 袋面粉中包含部分即将运抵的外国小麦。他补充说，其公司已订购 10,000 吨小麦，可生产约 350,000 袋面粉。

此类外国面粉的成本每袋至少为 13.50 美元。

主席表示，若将价格限定为 10 美元，而后又决定解除禁令，价格将会突然上涨。

何先生说，他不赞成固定价格。面粉供应更加充足会使价格下降。

孙乐斯先生说，并非指外国面粉的价格，因为正如主席所确认的那样，除汇率因素外，运费及其他费用均已上涨，且舱位难以获得。

回答主席时，孙乐斯先生表示，目前上海可用的面粉净总量约为 400,000 袋。

施先生指出，本地小麦商人不欲出售，正在等待更好的价格。回答约克（York）先生时，他说，这部分小麦中有一定数量储存在租界内。

何先生评论道，大约十天前，面粉的重置成本为每袋 11.60 美元至 11.70 美元，因为麦麸的销售收入足以覆盖面粉厂的运营开支。孙乐斯先生回答说

pages.en:
-8-
this is so only to a certain extent and repeats that freight has
gone up and tonnage is short.
The Chairman says that he hopes the Mills will see that
all available flour finds its way into the Settlement and he is
sure that if needed the aid of the Police will be given. Mr. Yorke
concurs.
Mr. Russell Sun states that Mill owners feel that in fair-
ness the Council should issue a statement in order to make it known
that foreign flour costs $13 per bag at present.
Replying to Mr. Ho, Mr. Russell Sun says that the daily
quota for Shanghai if increased would go to hoarders. He says the
daily local consumption for the past three years has never
approached the figure given by the Police (20,000 bags). He agrees
with the Chairman that 7,000 to 8,000 bags per day would be about
correct. He mentions that the present price of Flour at $10 per
bag is cheaper than the price for rice. There has been a far
greater rise in the price to consumers of that food.
Mr. Ho agrees but requests that Shanghai be given a
greater supply in order to keep the price within reasonable bounds.
Mr. Russell Sun says that apart from other factors, if
this is done Shanghai Mills would be exhausted and the cost of Flour
would then reach $15 per bag.
The Chairman remarks that no increase of Stocks to bring
about such a state is desired but just a little more is needed, say
a total of 10,000 bags daily for Shanghai.
Mr. Russell Sun repeats that the more free flour there is
the more will be exported from areas beyond the Council's control.
The Chairman says that this would be so unless steps can be taken
to prevent movement beyond the jurisdiction of the Settlement and
French Concession.
Mr. Russell Sun considers that 8,000 bags is sufficient
and should be the limit; his Company can allow 250,000 bags of Flour
for Shanghai needs for the next few months.
Mr. Ho says that he would be happy if Mr. Russell Sun would
make a larger offer and he would prefer him to say how much his
Company is prepared to allow daily for Shanghai.
pages.zh:
-8-
这种情况仅在某种程度上属实，并重申运费已上涨且吨位不足。
主席表示，他希望各面粉厂确保所有可用面粉均能运入租界，并确信如有需要，警方将提供协助。约克先生（Mr. Yorke）表示赞同。
孙乐斯尔先生（Mr. Russell Sun）指出，面粉厂主认为，为公平起见，工部局应发表声明，使公众知悉目前外国面粉每袋价格为13美元。
在回复何先生（Mr. Ho）时，孙乐斯尔先生表示，如果增加上海的每日配额，这些面粉将落入囤积者手中。他说，过去三年上海本地的每日消费量从未达到警方给出的数字（20,000袋）。他同意主席的看法，即每日7,000至8,000袋大致准确。他提到，目前面粉每袋10美元的价格比大米价格更便宜。而该食品对消费者的价格涨幅要大得多。
何先生表示同意，但要求增加对上海的供应，以便将价格保持在合理范围内。
孙乐斯尔先生表示，除其他因素外，如果这样做，上海的面粉厂库存将耗尽，届时面粉成本将达到每袋15美元。
主席评论说，并不希望因增加储备而导致这种局面，只是需要稍微多一点，例如上海每日总量为10,000袋。
孙乐斯尔先生重申，自由流通的面粉越多，从工部局管辖区域以外地区出口的面粉就越多。
主席表示，除非能采取步骤防止物资流动超出公共租界和法租界的管辖范围，否则情况确实会如此。
孙乐斯尔先生认为8,000袋已足够，并应作为上限；他的公司可在未来几个月内为上海的需求提供250,000袋面粉。
何先生表示，如果孙乐斯尔先生能提供更大的供应量，他将感到高兴，并且他更希望孙先生说明其公司准备每日允许向上海供应多少面粉。

pages.en:
-9-
. Mr. Russell Sun offers 5,000 bags of Flour daily up to a
total of 250,000 bags for Shanghai's requirements. Turning to Mr.
Sze, Mr. Ho enquires whether he is willing to allow a similar amount
from his Mills, to which Mr. Sze replies that he is unable to commit
his Company and remarks that his Company's stocks are low.
Mr. Ho says that supposing the Mills are prepared to supply
20,000 bags of Flour of 49 lbs. which the Police estimate is required
every day, then 980,000 people will get 1 lb. each a day, and since
the present estimated population is about 4 million, then the needs
of a quarter of the population will be met.
Mr. Sze repeats that he cannot commit his Company where-
upon Mr. Ho undertakes to make a personal appeal to Mr. Wang Yi-Ching,
General Manager of the Feh Sing Mills which Mr. Sze represents.
It is finally agreed
That the Mills will furnish the Police daily with lists of
shops showing their addresses and the quantity of Flour supplied
to them by the Mills.
In answer to Mr. Yorke, Mr. Sze says the lists would include about
100 shops.
In reply to the Chairman's query, Mr. Yorke says that the
Settlement Police will keep the French Police posted as to what has
been agreed and there will be close co-operation.
Replying to the Chairman on the matter of price, Mr.
Russell Sun states that he can only supply a total of 250,000 bags
of Flour at the rate of 5,000 bags daily for the next 50 days, and
the cost will be $10 per bag - this is at a great sacrifice.
Mr. Ho asks whether the retail prices should be fixed.
Mr. Russell Sun suggests that Retailers should sell at from $10.20
to $10.30 per bag of 49 lbs. He considers that 30 cents per bag is
a very good profit for them. Mr. Sze agrees.
The Chairman enquires what action will be taken against
hoarders and speculators. Mr. Yorke replies that if adequate proof
is forthcoming they would be charged.
pages.zh:
-9-
孙罗素（Russell Sun）先生提出，为满足上海的需求，每日供应面粉5,000袋，直至总量达到250,000袋。何先生转而询问施先生是否愿意从其米厂提供同等数量的面粉，施先生答复称他无法代表其公司作出承诺，并指出其公司库存偏低。

何先生表示，假设各米厂愿意供应警方估算的每日所需之49磅装面粉20,000袋，那么将有98万人每人每日获得1磅面粉；鉴于目前估计人口约为400万，这将满足四分之一人口的需求。

施先生重申他无法代表其公司作出承诺，于是何先生承诺将亲自向施先生所代表的丰兴米厂（Feh Sing Mills）总经理王义清（Wang Yi-Ching，音译）先生提出恳请。

最终议定：
各米厂将每日向警方提供一份商店清单，列明其地址以及米厂向其供应的面粉数量。

针对约克（Yorke）先生的提问，施先生表示该清单将包含约100家商店。

回应主席的询问，约克先生表示，租界警方将使法国警方随时知晓已达成的协议内容，并将保持密切合作。

就价格问题回复主席时，孙罗素先生声明，他在未来50天内仅能按每日5,000袋的速率供应总计250,000袋面粉，价格为每袋10美元——这是巨大的牺牲。

何先生询问是否应固定零售价格。

孙罗素先生建议零售商以每袋49磅面粉10.20至10.30美元的价格出售。他认为每袋30美分的利润对他们而言已相当丰厚。施先生表示同意。

主席询问将对囤积者和投机者采取何种行动。约克先生答复称，若有充分证据，将对他们提起诉讼。

pages.en:
-10-

Mr. Ho undertakes to get in touch with the retail dealers
through the Rice Guild since there is no Association of Flour shops
and most retailers also deal in Rice. He will inform them of what
has been decided.

Mr. Russell Sun expresses the hope that in order to
remove criticism the Council will give some publicity to what has
been promised.

The Chairman thanks Mr. Russell Sun and Mr. Szé for their
attendance and assistance.

The meeting terminates at 11.40 a.m.
pages.zh:
-10-

何先生承诺，由于不存在面粉店同业公会，且大多数零售商亦经营大米，故将通过米业公会与零售商人取得联系。他将向他们通报已作出的决定。

孙乐斯尔先生表示希望，为消除批评起见，工部局应对所承诺之事项予以公开宣传。

主席感谢孙乐斯尔先生及施先生（Szé）的出席与协助。

会议于上午11时40分结束。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT
80399/S(2)-H
12 3 H1

...S...L...Special Branch...Station. File No.................... Date March 11, 1941.

SUBJECT: Cheap Sale of Flour by Foh Sing Mill.

With reference to the attached cutting from
the China Press to the effect that the Foh Sing Flour
Mill will resume the cheap sale of flour from March 10,
enquiries proved the report to be correct, with the
exception of, the date mentioned.

In accordance with arrangements made by the
Shanghai Municipal Council, the Foh Sing Flour Mill
has, from time to time, sold flour at a cheap rate
to bona-fide consumers and food shops. The last cheap
sale, when the price of flour was $23.00 per bag, plus
30 cents commission for the authorized wholesalers, was
temporarily suspended towards the end of February.
Following further negotiations by the S.M.C., the mill
resumed cheap sales, from March 8, (not March 10 as
reported in the press) but the price was increased by
$2.00 per bag. The mill agreed to sell 5,873 bags daily,

March 17, 1940. Morning Translation.

Chinese-American Daily News, National Herald, Ta Mei Pao,
Central China Daily News, Circulation Daily News:

MACARONI SHOPS WANT CHEAP FLOUR

Following the steep rise in the price of rice,
the price of flour per bag recently rose to more than
$14, with the result that common people have been finding
it difficult to maintain their living.
Owing to the high cost price and the business
depression, local machine-made macaroni shop owners are
also experiencing much difficulty in preserving their
business. On February 24, they requested the S.M.C. to
supply cheap flour. In response to this request, the
Council made arrangements with the Foh Sin (福新) and
the Fu Foong (阜丰) flour mills to sell flour at $10.30
per bag to local machine-made macaroni shops. In all,
2,065 bags of flour have been supplied to these shops.
It is learned that the supply of cheap flour
will cease on March 19. Contending that this will
seriously affect the livelihood of the people as well as
the operation of their business, the machine-made macaroni
shops on March 15 detailed five representatives to approach
the Shanghai Chinese Chamber of Commerce asking it to
request the Council to continue the supply of such flour.
On the other hand, the Machine-made Flour Shop Owners'
Guild issued a notification to various members directing
them to register with the Guild regarding the quantity
of flour required daily.
Upon learning of this, more than 100 machine-
made macaroni shops, including those in Nantao, Chapei
and Hongkew, have applied for registration with the Guild
during the past two days.
It is learned that the S.M.C., in response to
the request to continue such supplies, is making further
arrangements with flour mills. It is also learned that
the quantity of flour to be supplied as well as the
period will be decided upon to-morrow.

机制面馆欲求廉价面粉

继米价急剧上涨之后，
近期每袋面粉价格已涨至14元以上，致使
普通民众难以维持生计。
由于成本高企及市面萧条，本地机制面馆店主
在维持经营方面也面临诸多困难。2月24日，他们请求工部局
供应廉价面粉。针对此项请求，公董局与福新（Foh Sin）和
阜丰（Fu Foong）面粉厂作出安排，以每袋10.30元的价格向本地机制面馆
出售面粉。共计已向这些面馆供应
2,065袋面粉。
据悉，廉价面粉的供应将于3月19日停止。机制面馆方面声称，此举将

另一方面，机制面粉店业主公会向各会员发布通知，责令

National Herald and Sin Wan Pao :-

MACARONI SHOP OWNERS WANT CHEAPER FLOUR

The following appeal was yesterday submitted to
the Chamber of Commerce by Wang Ching-wen (王錦文) and four
other representatives of the Shanghai Machine-Made Macaroni
Shop Owners' Guild :-
"Rice and flour have always been the staple food
of the people. In case of shortage of the former, the latter
is always used as a supplement. However, ever since the steep
rise in the prices of commodities, the people have been faced
with much difficulty in the maintenance of their livelihood,
while peace and order of the community have likewise been
affected.
"The present rise in the prices of commodities is
unprecedented in history. Fortunately a Commodity Prices
Readjustment Committee was established by the authorities to
undertake the prohibition of illegal enhancement of the prices
of commodities. Flour being one of the necessities for the
livelihood of the poor people, it naturally comes within the
category of commodities whose prices require adjustment by the
Committee.

"The enforcement of a price limit for rice
has been of much help to the poor people. Now there are
49 lbs of flour in one bag, thus the weight of four bags
of flour is equivalent to a picul of rice. With the price
of "kan-mee" rice fixed at $40 per picul, that of flour
should be $10 per bag. However, in private transactions of
late, the price of flour has risen as high as $14.70 per
bag. This is contrary to the adjusted prices of commodities
and affects the livelihood of the people.
"There are now more than 400 machine-made
macaroni shops in Shanghai upon which over 10,000 persons
are depending for livelihood. Every day they require a
supply of more than 4,000 bags of flour. As machine-made
macaroni is one of the staple foods of the people and more-
over as the cheap sale of flour is about to cease on
March 19, we, therefore, request your Chamber to approach
the authorities for the stabilization of the price of flour
and the procurement of further supplies of this commodity
so as to enable this trade to meet the requirements of the
public."

《国民新闻》与《新闻报》：

通心粉店主要求面粉降价

昨日，王锦文及上海机制通心粉店主同业公会其他四位代表向商会提交了如下请愿书：
“米与面历来为人民的主食。若前者短缺，后者常被用作补充。然而，自物价急剧上涨以来，民众在维持生计方面面临极大困难，社区的和平安宁亦因此受到影响。
“目前的物价上涨为历史所未见。幸而当局已成立物价调整委员会，负责禁止非法抬高物价。面粉既是贫民生活必需品之一，自然属于该委员会需调整价格的商品类别。

“实施大米限价对贫民大有裨益。目前每袋面粉重49磅，故四袋面粉之重量相当于一担大米。既然‘粘米’价格定为每担40元，则面粉价格应为每袋10元。然而，近期私下交易中，面粉价格已涨至每袋14.70元之高。此举违背了经调整的物价规定，并影响民众生计。
“上海现有机制通心粉店四百余家，逾万人赖此为生。每日需供应面粉四千余袋。鉴于机制通心粉乃人民主食之一，且廉价面粉销售将于3月19日停止，故此，我们恳请贵会向当局交涉，以稳定面粉价格并采购更多此类商品供应，从而使本行业能够满足公众需求。”

MARCH 11, 1942                          MORNING TRADE NEWS

Circulation Daily News and Sin Wen Pao :-

MACHINE-MADE MACARONI SHOPS APPEAL FOR RELIEF

Wang Ching-wen (王锦文), representative of
the Machine-Made Macaroni Trade Guild, was sent yesterday
to the Chinese Chamber of Commerce to appeal for relief.
The Chamber of Commerce answered Wang that Mr. T.K. □,
the Deputy Secretary of the S.M.C., had already asked the
flour mills concerned to continue supplying flour to various
traders at a cheap price and that as soon as a decision can
be arrived at for conducting the cheap sale of flour, a
notice will be issued accordingly.
It is learned that the Machine-Made Macaroni
Trade Guild has notified all the macaroni shops that after
the suspension of the cheap sale of flour on March 19,
business will be carried on as usual and that if obliged to
do so they may raise the sale price in order to continue
selling at their shops.

cents in the afternoon on the pretext that only 5 bags of fixed
price flour were obtained daily, which is hardly enough to an-
swer the demands of all. But we do not know where this extra
high priced flour comes from. It has been found that there is
a room on the first floor of the shop, in which several hundred
bags of flour were hoarded last winter, and the time he bought
it, the price was only seven dollars odd per bag. Since there
is an order to fixing the price, how can he raise the price,
and can he cause a breach of the rules as he himself is a re-
presentative. We therefore request you kindly to make an ins-
pection in order to prove what we said is true. Furthermore,
he has been the foreman of Yu Foong Cotton Factory, and now
he has been appointed the foreman of the Carpenter's Room of
Sing On Cotton Factory, Woosung, and besides he is quite in-
fluential. For your information, we have also written to the
Shanghai Chamber of Commerce, the Deputy Secretary Ho, asking
for the investigation of the same, and at the same time we
have notified the said Guild, requesting for an investigation
notice!

Signed,
The
People living in Sun Ka Tan, Yangtsepoo.

Secretariat,

March 8, 1940.

R.". Yorke, Esq.,
Deputy Commissioner of Police.

Dear Mr. Yorke,

Mr. Liang Ying-tsoon, Manager of the Nee
Loong Cereal Shop, 737 Boone Road, called on me yesterday
at 5:30 p.m. and explained the difficulties his shop was
encountering in dealing with certain loafers who repeated
purchases of cheap flour from his shop daily.

He agreed that the daily cheap sale of 50
bags of flour should continue at his shop until March 19
as previously arranged. He requested, however, that the
system of distribution might be amended in the following
manner:-

That his shop be permitted to distribute,
in the presence of the Police, to each person in
the queue tickets entitling the holder to buy a
bag of flour from his shop on the date stated on
the ticket upon payment of $10.30. The number
of tickets issued at any one time shall not
exceed 200, and the sale is limited to 50 bags
per day. This scheme has the advantage of afford-
ing every 50 persons in the waiting line a chance
of buying, and removing the present abominable
racket of the first few in the queue to repeat
purchases every day. The tickets will be made by
the shop in such a way that no imitation is
possible.

I hope that this suggestion will commend
itself to you.

Yours sincerely,

R. 约克先生（R. Yorke, Esq.），
警务处副总监。

尊敬的约克先生：

布恩路737号“尼隆”粮行（Nee Loong Cereal Shop）经理梁英春（Liang Ying-tsoon，音译）先生于昨日下午5时30分来访，向本人说明了该店在应对某些游手好闲之徒每日重复购买廉价面粉时所遇到的困难。

他同意按照先前的安排，其店铺每日廉价出售50袋面粉的做法应持续至3月19日。然而，他请求对分发制度作如下修改：

准许其店铺在警察在场的情况下，向排队中的每人发放票券，持券人可在票券所示日期支付10.30元后，从其店铺购买一袋面粉。每次发出的票券数量不得超过200张，且每日销售量限制为50袋。此方案的优势在于，能使排队等候的每50人都有购买机会，并消除目前排在队伍最前面的几个人每天重复购买的恶劣舞弊行为。票券将由该店以无法仿制的方式制作。

我希望这项建议能蒙您采纳。

此致
敬礼

Enquiries show that the measure, recently
introduced, whereby macaroni, wheatcake and noodle
shops would sell flour in small quantities to the
public, has not met with the success it deserved.
Certain of the shops in question have been
visited and it appears that the number of bags
received from the distributors is insufficient
to enable the shop owner to sell flour and at the
same time to carry on his normal retail business
of selling noodles, macaroni, etc. His primary
interest being the sale of manufactured and cooked
foods the owner, therefore, utilises the major
portion of his quota of flour for this purpose.
The remainder, after his requirements for noodles,
etc., have been filled, he is prepared to sell in
lots, seldom exceeding a pound in weight, so small
that they are of little use to anyone.
Despite the fact that only insignificant
quantities of loose flour are being sold by the food
shops, it must be remembered that the poorer classes
are, nevertheless, benefitting to the extent that
cooked wares, noodles, etc. are to be purchased at
a price lower than has been in force during recent
weeks.

Misc. 142/40.

1.

Unrest amongst coolies at the Poh Shing Flour Mill.

At 10-30am. on 1/3/40 S.I. Ching visited a
Flour Shop at No.480 Shanhaikwan Road where flour was
to be sold cheaply to the public, and learned that
the flour had not been delivered from the Poh Shing
Flour Mill, West Soochow Road, as arranged.

S.I. Ching then visited this Mill, and found that
approximately 150 coolies employed there to load the
motor trucks had refused to work.

The Station was informed and C.D.S. 193 and
the undersigned attended and obtained the following
particulars:-

It has been the custom during the past few months
for the management to allow these coolies the purchase
of flour at a cheap rate, but as this cheap flour is
now being sold to the public, this practice has been dis-
continued and the workers have been given "Rice money"
of 40 cents per day. On 29/2/40 the coolies asked for
the cheap flour and were told that this could only be
sold to them at one Dollar cheaper than the outside
price. This resulted in the coolies refusing to load
the cheap flour on the morning of 1/3/40.

Later however the coolies resumed work, pending
further negotiations.

D.C. (Special Branch) informed.
Dr. Watson

1.

波兴面粉厂苦力中的不安情绪。

1940年3月1日上午10时30分，巡长郑（Ching）走访了山海关路480号的一家面粉店，该店原定以低价向公众出售面粉，但他获悉，按照约定，面粉并未从西苏州路的波兴面粉厂运抵。

随后，巡长郑前往该面粉厂，发现受雇于该厂负责装载卡车的约150名苦力拒绝工作。

警局接到通知后，第193号中国籍侦探警司及本人赶赴现场，并查得以下详情：

在过去几个月里，厂方惯例允许这些苦力以低价购买面粉，但由于目前这种低价面粉正面向公众出售，该做法已停止，改为向工人发放每日40分的“米贴”。1940年2月29日，苦力们要求购买低价面粉，但被告知只能以比市价低一美元的价格卖给他们。这导致苦力们在1940年3月1日上午拒绝装载低价面粉。

不过，后来苦力们恢复了工作，以待进一步谈判。

尊敬的先生：

我们下列签署人“上海宝兴路330号卡尔萨迪万委员会”，谨恳请阁下设法获取五十袋小麦面粉，这些面粉正以专为穷人设定的特别低价出售。

该廉价面粉销售点开设在受贵警队管辖的外国租界内，我方一些印度同胞前往购买，但因人群拥挤无法靠近大门，事实上，我方一名同胞还遭扒窃。

印度社群向我们提出请求，希望向阁下呈递请愿书，以便为他们安排一种更便捷获取面粉的方式。

先生，您非常清楚，印度巡捕的工资微薄，仅够维持生计，我方部分同胞在此有家眷，生活极为艰难，因此我们迫于形势不得不购买廉价面粉。最后，我们再次恳请并敦促阁下为印度民众设定购买廉价面粉的特定日期和时间。

对于给您带来的麻烦，我们预先深表感谢，并希望阁下能考虑此事。

您忠实的仆人，
卡尔萨迪万秘书

Sir,
Following upon your interview with the Secretary-
General yesterday, I consulted with Mr. Gubb and Mr. T.K. Ho
at 11 a.m. today. Mr. Gubb who is most sympathetically
inclined towards the Police view succeeded in persuading
Mr. Ho that the continual sale of flour in 49lb bags
would not alleviate the position of the poor. It trans-
pired during this interview that Mr. Ho had, prior to
arranging for the sale of flour in 49-lb bags, made some
enquiries regarding containers in which smaller quantities
of flour could be retailed from the shops. The cost of
paper bags and some difficulty in having such bags made
locally convinced Mr. Ho that the sale in small quantities
was not practicable.
After a lengthy discussion it was decided by
Mr. Gubb that if the police could devise ways and means
of having flour retailed in smaller quantities without
incurring any expense, such ways and means could be adopted
forthwith.
I learn from Mr. Ho this afternoon that he is
introducing a measure of relief which may be of sufficient
benefit to the poorer classes to obviate any further action.
Two shops situated in the French Concession and one
in the Settlement, hitherto selling flour totalling 2,000
bags daily, will, commencing from February 24, cease to
sell. The 2,000 bags of flour will be delivered direct to
302 noodle, macaroni and wheatcake shops and the proprietors
of these shops have given an undertaking to Mr. Ho to sell
flour loosely in quantities as small as 2 lbs.

致警务处长：
阁下昨日与秘书长会晤后，我于今日上午11时与古布先生（Mr. Gubb）及何德奎先生（Mr. T.K. Ho）进行了磋商。古布先生对警方的观点深表同情，他成功说服了何先生，使其相信继续以49磅袋装形式出售面粉并不能缓解穷人的处境。在此次会谈中获悉，何先生在安排以49磅袋装形式出售面粉之前，曾就商店零售较小数量面粉所需的容器问题进行过一些调查。纸袋的成本以及 locally 制作此类袋子的某些困难，使何先生确信小量销售并不可行。
经过长时间讨论，古布先生决定，如果警方能够想出办法在不产生任何费用的情况下实现面粉的小量零售，则可立即采纳这些办法。
我今天下午从何先生处得知，他正在推行一项救济措施，其益处可能足以惠及贫困阶层，从而无需采取进一步行动。
此前每日共计出售2,000袋面粉的两家位于法租界的商店和一家位于本租界的商店，将从2月24日起停止销售。这2,000袋面粉将直接运送给302家面条、通心粉和麦饼店，这些店的店主已向何先生承诺，将以散装形式出售面粉，最小售卖量为2磅。

February 20, 1940.
Sales of Cheap Flour
---------------------

At 2.30 p.m. on 19th February 1940, a meeting
convened by Mr. T. K. Ho, Deputy Secretary, was
held in the Council Chamber and was attended by Mr. Ho,
the Municipal Police represented by Mr. Yorke, Mr.
Samson and Mr. Sharman, and the French Police
represented by Mons. Moret and Mons. Emilianoff.

The local flour situation was discussed with
particular reference to the sale of cheap flour which,
in accordance with the agreement reached between
the mill owners and the dealers, began in both
Settlement and Concession on Monday, February 19th.
The flour disposed of thus, it appeared, was not
passing into the hands of that section of the public
intended to benefit by the low rate at which it was
offered but, instead, was being sold to loafers and
agents who were, in turn, retailing it at excess
profits.

Police representatives described the situation
that existed at the flour shops in their respective
districts and put forward suggestions which they
considered might nullify the activities of profiteers
and at the same time facilitate the handling of
the large and, in some cases, disorderly crowds which
had attended the shops in question.

Mr. Samson in whose district crowds had been
largest and most unruly, said that amongst the
buyers there was a large preponderance of loafers
who were quite obviously not purchasing on their own
behalf and who, when stocks were at length exhausted,
led the people in throwing stones and mud. Mr.
Samson further stated that the presence of such
pages.zh:
1940年2月20日。
廉价面粉销售情况
---------------------

1940年2月19日下午2时30分，由副秘书何先生（T. K. Ho）召集的会议在工部局议事厅举行。出席会议者有何先生，警务处代表约克先生（Yorke）、萨姆森先生（Samson）和谢尔曼先生（Sharman），以及法租界巡捕房代表莫雷先生（Mons. Moret）和埃米利亚诺夫先生（Mons. Emilianoff）。

会议讨论了本地面粉供应状况，特别关注廉价面粉的销售问题。根据面粉厂主与经销商之间达成的协议，此类面粉于2月19日（星期一）起在公共租界及法租界同时开始发售。据观察，以此方式处置的面粉并未流入旨在从低价中受益的那部分公众手中，反而被售予游手好闲之徒及代理人，这些人随后以超额利润进行零售。

警方代表描述了各自辖区内面粉店存在的状况，并提出了若干建议。他们认为这些建议既能遏制投机商的活动，又能有助于应对涌入相关店铺的大批人群，且在某些情况下，这些人群秩序混乱。

萨姆森先生所在辖区的人群规模最大且最为不守秩序，他指出，购买者中绝大多数显然是游手好闲之徒，他们并非为自己购买，而当库存最终耗尽时，这些人便煽动民众投掷石块和泥土。萨姆森先生进一步指出，此类人员的存在

pages.en:
- 2 -

large crowds, over 5,000 persons at one shop on North
Chekiang Road, could, in some measures, be attributed
to the fact that because deliveries from the mill
were late in arrival, a great many people had
assembled before sales began.

Mr. Sharman reported conditions similar to those
described by Mr. Samson and dwelt at length on the
circumstances which enabled profiteers, acting with
the aid of loafers, to obtain flour intended for
the poorer classes.

Monsieur Meret, representative of the French
Police, also referred to large crowds and the difficulty
in handling them occasioned by the inconvenient
situation of certain of the flour shops. He mentioned
the fact that some 200 bags of flour purchased at
the special rate had that morning been transferred
to Nantao where undoubtedly they had been retailed
at a large profit.

Suggestions for dealing with this reported
profiteering were requested by Mr. Ho and, in
response, it was proposed by Mr. Sharman that before
a bag of flour could be sold, the buyer must produce
a Municipal Council rate receipt, thus proving that
he was either a ratepayer or his representative. On
concluding the sale the receipt would be endorsed on
the reverse side with particulars as regards the

February 20, 40

At 2.30 p.m. on 19th February 1940, a meeting
convened by Mr. T. K. Ho, Deputy Secretary, was
held in the Council Chamber and was attended by Mr. Ho,
the Municipal Police represented by Mr. Yorke, Mr.
Samson and Mr. Sharman, and the French Police
represented by Mons. Meret and Mons. Emilianoff.

The local flour situation was discussed with
particular reference to the sale of cheap flour which,
in accordance with the agreement reached between
the mill owners and the dealers, began in both
Settlement and Concession on Monday, February 19th.
The flour disposed of thus, it appeared, was not
passing into the hands of that section of the public
intended to benefit by the low rate at which it was
offered but, instead, was being sold to loafers and
agents who were, in turn, retailing it at excess
profits.

Police representatives described the situation
that existed at the flour shops in their respective
districts and put forward suggestions which they
considered might nullify the activities of profiteers
and at the same time facilitate the handling of
the large and, in some cases, disorderly crowds which
had attended the shops in question.

February 17, 1940.

Commissioner of Police.

Sales of cheap flour

At 2.15 p.m. 16/2/40, a meeting convened
by Mr. T.K. Ho, Deputy Secretary, was held in the
Council Chamber and attended by Mr. Ho, his staff,
representatives of the French and Municipal Police
Forces and about 40 Chinese dealers and shop-keepers.

Mr. Ho explained the extreme necessity of
keeping prices at a minimum and measures to amelior-
ate present condition in re: flour were discussed.
The following points were agreed upon:-

The management of the Poh Sing and Fou
Foong Flour Mills agreed to supply 7,500 bags of
flour daily for sale and consumption solely in Shanghai.
The Poh Sing Mill will supply 2,500 bags and the Fou
Foong 5,000 bags daily. The price ex-mill will be
$10 per bag effective from February 18; this price
will remain fixed for a period of one month when the
managements of the mills will review and reconsider
their prices.

All wholesale and retail dealers have in
turn agreed to sell this flour at $10.30 per bag and
to do their utmost to ensure that no person purchases
more than one bag per day. Sales on the lines enumer-
ated above will commence on Monday February 19 in 17
(including 3 on O.O.L. roads) shops situated in the
Settlement and 10 shops situated in the Concession
as per lists attached herewith.

Shops will open for business daily at 9 a.m.
and continue until 12 noon. If stocks are not then
exhausted, sales will continue in the afternoon, com-
mencing from 1.30 p.m. until stocks are exhausted.

It is difficult to estimate the length of
time each shop will be engaged in the sale of this
cheap flour daily, but some idea can be gained from
pages.zh:
1940年2月17日。

警务处处长。

廉价面粉销售事宜

1940年2月16日下午2时15分，由副总办何德奎（T.K. Ho）先生召集的会议在工部局议事厅举行。出席会议者包括何先生及其职员、法租界巡捕房与公共租界工部局警务处的代表，以及约40名华商经销商和店主。

何先生阐述了将价格维持在最低水平的极端必要性，并讨论了改善当前面粉状况的措施。达成如下共识：

宝兴面粉厂（Poh Sing Flour Mills）和福丰面粉厂（Fou Foong Flour Mills）的管理层同意每日供应7,500袋面粉，专供上海地区销售和消费。其中，宝兴面粉厂每日供应2,500袋，福丰面粉厂每日供应5,000袋。出厂价为每袋10元，自2月18日起生效；该价格固定一个月，届时各厂管理层将对价格进行审查和重新考量。

所有批发和零售经销商依次同意以每袋10.30元的价格出售此面粉，并尽力确保每人每天购买不超过一袋。上述所列的销售方式将于2月19日（星期一）开始实施，涉及位于公共租界内的17家店铺（其中包括位于越界筑路区域的3家）以及位于法租界内的10家店铺，具体名单附后。

各店铺每日上午9时开门营业，持续至中午12时。若届时库存未售罄，下午将继续销售，从下午1时30分开始，直至库存售完为止。

难以估算每家店铺每日销售这种廉价面粉所需的时间长短，但可以从

February 20, 40
Sales of Cheap Flour.

At 2.30 p.m. on 19th February 1940, a meeting
convened by Mr. T. A. Ho, Deputy Secretary, was
held in the Council Chamber and was attended by Mr. Ho,
the Municipal Police represented by Mr. Yorke, Mr.
Samson and Mr. Sharman, and the French Police
represented by Mons. Moret and Mons. Emilianoff.

The local flour situation was discussed with
particular reference to the sale of cheap flour which,
in accordance with the agreement reached between
the mill owners and the dealers, began in both
Settlement and Concession on Monday, February 19th.
The flour disposed of thus, it appeared, was not
passing into the hands of that section of the public
intended to benefit by the low rate at which it was
offered but, instead, was being sold to loafers and
agents who were, in turn, retailing it at excess
profits.

Police representatives described the situation
that existed at the flour shops in their respective
districts and put forward suggestions which they
considered might nullify the activities of profiteers
and at the same time facilitate the handling of
the large and, in some cases, disorderly crowds which
had attended the shops in question.

Mr. Samson in whose district crowds had been
largest and most unruly, said that amongst the
pages.zh:
1940年2月20日

廉价面粉销售事宜。

1940年2月19日下午2时30分，由副总办何先生（Mr. T. A. Ho）召集的会议在工部局议事厅举行。出席会议者有何先生；公共租界警务处代表约克先生（Mr. Yorke）、萨姆森先生（Mr. Samson）和夏曼先生（Mr. Sharman）；以及法租界警务处代表莫雷先生（Mons. Moret）和埃米利亚诺夫先生（Mons. Emilianoff）。

会议讨论了本地面粉供应情况，特别提及根据磨坊主与经销商之间达成的协议，于2月19日（星期一）在公共租界及法租界同时开始的廉价面粉销售。据显示，以此方式处置的面粉并未流入旨在从低价中受益的那部分公众手中，反而被出售给游手好闲之徒及代理商，这些人随后以超额利润进行零售。

警方代表描述了各自辖区内面粉店存在的状况，并提出了他们认为既能遏制投机商活动，又能有助于应对光顾相关店铺的大批且有时混乱无序的人群的建议。

萨姆森先生所在辖区的人群规模最大且最为不守秩序，他表示，在……

pages.en:
-2-

buyers there was a large preponderance of loafers
who were quite obviously not purchasing on their own
behalf and who, when stocks were at length exhausted,
led the people in throwing stones and mud. Mr.
Samson further stated that the presence of such
large crowds, over 5,000 persons at one shop on North
Chekiang Road, could, in some measure, be attributed
to the fact that because deliveries from the mill
were late in arrival, a great many people had
assembled before sales began.

Mr. Sharman reported conditions similar to those
described by Mr. Samson and dwelt at length on the
circumstances which enabled profiteers, acting with
the aid of loafers, to obtain flour intended for
the poorer classes.

Monsieur Moret, representative of the French
Police, also referred to large crowds and the difficulty
in handling them occasioned by the inconvenient
situation of certain of the flour shops. He mentioned
the fact that some 200 bags of flour purchased at
the special rate had that morning been transferred
to Nantao where undoubtedly they had been retailed
at a large profit.

Suggestions for dealing with this reported
profiteering were requested by Mr. Ho and, in
response, it was proposed by Mr. Sharman that before
a bag of flour could be sold, the buyer must produce

买家之中，游手好闲之徒占绝大多数，这些人显然并非为自己购买，而当库存最终耗尽时，他们便煽动民众投掷石块和泥土。萨姆森先生（Mr. Samson）进一步指出，如此庞大的人群——仅浙江北路一家店铺前就聚集了超过5,000人——在某种程度上可归因于面粉厂交货迟到，导致许多人在开售前便已聚集等候。

夏曼先生（Mr. Sharman）报告的情况与萨姆森先生所述类似，并详细阐述了使投机商在游手好闲者的协助下，得以获取本应供应给贫困阶层的面粉的各种情形。

法国警务处代表莫雷先生（Monsieur Moret）也提及人群拥挤以及因部分面粉店位置不便而导致的管控困难。他提到，当天上午，以特价购买的约200袋面粉已被转运至南市，无疑在那里以高额利润进行零售。

何先生（Mr. Ho）要求提出应对上述 Reported 投机行为的建议，作为回应，夏曼先生提议，在出售每袋面粉之前，购买者必须出示

he was either a ratepayer or his representative. On
concluding the sale the receipt would be endorsed on
the reverse side with particulars as regards the
amount and the date when purchased. The buyer

The above suggestion was criticised by Mr.
Yorke on the grounds that, again, the poorer classes
would not benefit. Flour would be bought by the
rate-paying tenant of a premises but it was very
doubtful whether he would be prepared to distribute
it, except at a profit, among his needy sub-tenants.
Mr. Yorke then put forward the suggestion
that the sale of flour in quantities greatly reduced
would go far towards solving the problem and would
result in a better distribution of the commodity

if flour was sold in quantities of 5 lbs. or 10 lbs.
instead of in bags at 49 lbs, the standard weight,

Yorke further pointed out that the $10.30 required

could ill afford, but that the dollar and few odd
cents necessary for 5 lbs. was much more likely to be

that the mill machinery was adapted only to the size

Speaking of the reports concerning the disorderly
